# How to annotate {#sec-how-to-annotate}

This script is a living document. It was drafted with the help of generative
AI from the lecturer's own teaching material, then reviewed and edited by the
lecturer - and it is improved every week by **you**. When you find an error,
an unclear passage, or a better example, you annotate it directly in the text
with [Hypothesis](https://web.hypothes.is/). The lecturer reads every
annotation, answers questions, and merges corrections into the next version.

Annotating is not optional extra work. It is part of the coursework
(arbeidskrav), it is the fastest way to get an error fixed for everyone, and
it trains the one skill you will need most when working with AI-generated
material in practice: checking whether it is right.

## Why you should do this

- **You understand it better.** You cannot check a passage without
  understanding it. Annotating a chapter is the difference between having
  read it and knowing it.
- **The script gets better - for you.** Every error you flag is fixed before
  the exam. You are improving the text you will revise from in December, not
  next year's.
- **I need your help.** I cannot read my own text with fresh eyes, and I
  cannot try every step in every session the way you do. You are the only
  ones who see where it fails.
- **It is the skill of your job.** AI-drafted text is now the norm in
  security work and in research writing. Checking it, and saying precisely what is
  wrong, is what you will be paid for.
- **It is safe.** The group is private. A wrong correction is not a mistake;
  it starts a discussion, and that is worth as much as a correct one.
- **You get credit.** Merged contributions are named in the changelog, and
  the annotations are your arbeidskrav - done at the moment you were reading
  anyway.

You can write in **English or Norwegian**, whichever you think faster in.

::: {.callout-note}
## One honest word

I know this is a lot on top of everything else, and I know this is "only" a
methods course next to your thesis and your other ones. But this time I really need your
help. I can write the script; I cannot test it from where you sit. Nobody
else will find the places where it fails you - that is you, this semester.
Two annotations per chapter, five minutes each. That is the whole ask. - Timo
:::

## When to annotate

Annotate whenever the text does not do its job - **not only while reading
before the session, but also while answering the questions for discussion and the exercises at the end of a chapter, and while writing the essay**. If a definition, a worked example or a step in the running example does not hold up, or the text does not give you what you need for your own Part I to IV,
that is exactly the annotation we want. Annotate the passage that failed you,
say what you were trying to do, and what happened instead.

Good moments to annotate:

- while reading a chapter before the session - questions and unclear passages
- during the session - things that were explained differently than written
- **while answering the questions for discussion and the exercises at the end of a chapter, and while writing your essay** - definitions, worked examples and steps that do not work for your own topic
- after the session - a real-world example or a source that would make the
  passage better

## Set up once

Annotations for this course live in the **private group IKT 448 2026**. Nobody
outside the group can see them.

1. Create a free account at [hypothes.is/signup](https://hypothes.is/signup)
   - use your UiA e-mail. Your username is visible to other group
   members; it does not have to be your real name.
2. While signed in, open the group page
   [hypothes.is/groups/XjreopNx/ikt-448-2026](https://hypothes.is/groups/XjreopNx/ikt-448-2026)
   and click **Join group**.
3. Open any page of this script. The Hypothesis sidebar sits at the right
   edge of the page (the small `<` tab). Open it, sign in, and **switch the
   selector at the top from *Public* to *IKT 448 2026***.

The sidebar remembers the group per browser, not per site. Check the
selector before every post - it takes one second.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Public does not count

Anything posted to *Public* is readable by the whole internet under your
username and does **not** count for the course. If you posted to Public by
mistake: open the annotation, delete it, and post it again in the group.
:::

## Annotate

1. Select the passage with the mouse. A small popup appears: choose
   **Annotate** (not *Highlight* - highlights carry no text and no tag and do
   not count).
2. Write your comment. For a correction: what is wrong, what is right, and
   where you got it from (article, page in Oates, or what you observed).
3. Add exactly one **tag** in the *Add tags* field: `question`, `correction`
   or `practice example`. Type it and press Enter.
4. Check the group selector, then click **Post to IKT 448 2026**.
5. To respond to someone else's annotation, use **Reply** under it. Replies
   are welcome and visible to the lecturer, but they do not count as your own
   annotation.

## What counts as a substantive annotation

Annotations are counted on substance, not volume. Three kinds count:

- **Question** - a genuine question about the passage that a fellow student
  could learn from seeing answered. "I don't get this" does not count;
  "does X also hold when Y, given what the previous section says about Z?"
  does.
- **Correction** - a factual, technical, or editorial error in the text,
  with a short justification and, where relevant, a source. A step that
  fails in practice counts as a correction if you say what happened.
- **Practice example** - a concrete worked example, counter-example, or
  real-world case that illustrates the passage, described precisely enough
  that it could be merged into the script.


Three examples of what a counted annotation looks like:

| Tag | Where | Annotation |
|---|---|---|
| `question` | Chapter 6, on "convenience sampling is legitimate if named" | Does that also hold when the whole sample comes from one employer? Chapter 8 calls the same situation a census of one organisation and says to generalise analytically, not statistically. Which of the two applies to the running example with six partner firms? |
| `correction` | Chapter 10, on "notify SIKT before data collection starts" | SIKT asks for the notification at least 30 days before collection begins, and the assessment can take longer in busy periods. "Before" reads as if the day before were enough; the lead time matters for the essay timeline and should be stated. |
| `practice example` | Chapter 9, on probing in semi-structured interviews | In my pilot interview the question "how do reviews typically go in your team?" got a one-word answer until I followed up with "tell me about the last one". The episode question did what the general one could not. Good example for the broken/repaired table. |

Not substantive: "+1" or agreement notes, restating the text, formatting
complaints without a fix, or duplicating an existing annotation (read the
thread first).

**Quota:** two substantive annotations per student per chapter. Annotations on
any chapter count; spreading them across chapters is encouraged.

## What happens to your annotations

- The lecturer goes through the group every week, replies to questions, and
  decides on corrections. Accepted corrections go into the next version of
  the script; you will see your fix in the text, usually within a week.
- Merged contributions are credited in `CHANGELOG.md` - one line per
  contribution, with your username or a handle of your choice.
- Larger contributions (a full worked example, a new exercise, a
  glossary entry) follow the co-authorship flow in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- Your annotation stays yours in Hypothesis. The merged text becomes part of
  the script under the script's licence (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).
- Annotations in the group are visible to group members only - the lecturer
  and your fellow students in IKT448. They are not public and are not
  indexed by search engines.

## If something does not work

- **No group in the selector** - you have not joined it yet, or you are not
  signed in. Open the group link above and click *Join group*.
- **Highlights do not show up** - reload the page once; the sidebar sometimes
  loads before the text does.
- **Posted to Public** - delete and repost in the group (see above).
- **The passage is in an image or a code box** - annotate the nearest line
  of text and say which figure or command you mean.
